subject: QuantLine discovery — SLOs, model fit, and topology recap

Subject: QuantLine discovery — SLOs, model fit, and topology recap

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call so we all have the same list of constraints, assumptions, and next actions. I tried to capture the pain, the goals, and an initial topology that we can iterate on.

Pain points you highlighted:
- High 95/99 tail for short prompts (customer-facing autocomplete): spikes above 600ms at peak; % of timed-out requests impacting UX.
- Bursty nightly ingestion (batch scoring) that needs sustained throughput without disrupting real-time traffic.
- Data sensitivity: some requests contain PII that must not leave QuantLine VPC.

Goals / SLOs stated on the call:
- Real-time: 95th < 200ms, 99th < 350ms for prompts <= 64 tokens (typical autocomplete/intent).
- Batch: sustain 200 req/s for long-running scoring jobs (up to 512 tokens) during nightly windows.
- Uptime target: 99.95% for the inference surface; graceful fallback to lower-cost model if primary unavailable.

Model and workload notes we captured:
- Primary: QuantLine fine-tuned Llama-13B (sensitive).
- Fallback / reranking: Llama-7B fine-tuned (less PII) for bulk scoring and fallback.
- Typical prompt length distribution attached (see sample-payloads.jsonl and latency-sample.csv).

Initial deployment topology (proposed):
- Private VPC deployment using Redwood Private control plane (customer-managed networking).
- Dedicated pool: 3x A100-equivalent GPU nodes for low-latency real-time traffic with KV cache shared across nodes.
- Separate batch pool (2x larger instance types) isolated by autoscaler to handle nightly throughput bursts.
- Route-based policy: real-time requests -> low-latency pool; bulk -> batch pool; fallback policy to small hosted instances for degraded cases.

Optimization suggestions (quick):
- KV/prefix caching for common autocomplete prefixes to reduce token work.
- Quantization path for fallback model (int8) to reduce memory and allow denser packing on batch nodes.
- Batching windows with dynamic size for batch pool; keep real-time serving continuous batching tuned to 5-8ms targets to avoid latency spikes.

Attachments: quantline-mpa-draft.pdf (MPA skeleton for procurement), sample-payloads.jsonl, latency-sample.csv.

Next steps we proposed on the call (please confirm):
1) QuantLine to share representative sample payloads, and an IP allowlist for our tech kickoff.
2) We do a 2-week pilot: smoke tests + a 72-hour latency soak at representative load (mutual action plan in the attached PDF).
3) QuantLine to provide SOC2 questionnaire answers or a point of contact for compliance evidence.
4) Schedule a technical kickoff with your infra and security folks next week (proposed windows below).

Proposed windows (PST): Tue 9/28 10:00–11:00, Wed 9/29 14:00–15:00. Let me know which works and if you need a different timezone.

Thanks — happy to adjust this summary if I missed anything.

— Kimberly

Thanks Kimberly — this is a helpful write-up. A few clarifications and confirmations from our side: 

- Confirming the 95/99 targets you listed are our priority for the product-facing endpoint (autocomplete).
- For batch scoring: the 200 req/s is an average sustained rate during the nightly window; we do see short spikes to ~400 req/s for up to 10 minutes.
- Data residency: PII must remain in our VPC. We can provide a temporary read-only S3 bucket inside our VPC and an allowlist for IPs.

On the compliance ask: we can share SOC2 artifact summaries but need to scope which logs are allowed to be accessed by Redwood during the pilot. Our security lead (Tom) will confirm the audit window and redaction requirements.

We are available for the Tue 9/28 10:00 PST slot for the kickoff — please send a calendar invite.

On attachments: I uploaded an extra file (example-configs.yml) to the Drive link — please check.

Elena

Subject: Re: QuantLine discovery — SLOs, model fit, and topology recap (internal notes)

Internal: quick technical notes for the kickoff — saving these here so we bring the right data.

1) Topology sketch (proposal) — real-time pool: 3x gpus w/ NVMe KV cache replication. Batch pool: 2x larger instances with autoscaler; isolate network egress.
2) Quantization: aim to run Llama-7B int8 for fallback; validate FSDP/quant path on one node during smoke run.
3) Batching config: real-time should use micro-batching (dynamic) targeting median latency 30–50ms and 95th under 200ms. Batch pool: aggressive batching, limit max latency 2s (acceptable for scoring).
4) Telemetry we need up-front: sample p95/p99 distributions, token lengths, and representative error cases. Request sample heatmap from Elena ahead of kickoff.

Also: propose an on-call window during the 72-hour soak to triage any KV cache thrash. If we can get SSH into a bastion in their VPC that will speed diagnostics.

— Karthik
